stem: The student wants to present the aim of Ferrer's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• At the site of Tambo Viejo in Peru, archaeologists uncovered dozens of circular stone storage buildings.
• Researchers had long disagreed about whether the buildings once held grain or dried meat.
• In 2022, archaeologist Lucía Ferrer led a team that sought to determine what had been stored in the buildings.
• The team analyzed chemical residues preserved in the buildings' clay floors.
• They detected traces of maize starch in nearly every building.
choices: Ferrer's team detected traces of maize starch in nearly every one of the circular stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Ferrer's 2022 study sought to determine what had been stored in the circular stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Ferrer's team analyzed chemical residues preserved in the clay floors of the stone buildings at Tambo Viejo.
Researchers had long disagreed about whether the stone buildings at Tambo Viejo held grain or dried meat.
explanation: The goal asks for the aim, meaning the purpose or question behind the study. Choice B uses the note saying Ferrer's team "sought to determine what had been stored in the buildings," so it states exactly what the study set out to learn.

A.why: You picked the study's finding. That is the result, not the aim. The goal asked what the team wanted to find out, not what it discovered.

C.why: You picked the method. Analyzing floor residues is how the team did the study, not why it did it.

D.why: You picked the background. This is the disagreement that came before the study, and it never mentions Ferrer's study or what it set out to do.

stem: The student wants to present the conclusion of Okafor's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Small earthquakes sometimes occur in tight clusters called swarms.
• Seismologist Daniel Okafor investigated whether swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were caused by moving underground fluids.
• His team placed 40 seismometers across the ridge and monitored them for 18 months.
• The instruments recorded more than 6,000 small earthquakes.
• The team concluded that the swarms were triggered by water migrating upward through cracks in the rock.
choices: Okafor's team placed 40 seismometers across Haldane Ridge and monitored them for a period of 18 months.
Okafor investigated whether earthquake swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were caused by moving underground fluids.
Over 18 months, seismometers on Haldane Ridge recorded more than 6,000 small earthquakes in swarms.
Okafor's team concluded that the swarms beneath Haldane Ridge were triggered by water rising through cracks in rock.
explanation: The goal asks for the conclusion, so you need the stage where the researchers say what their results mean. Choice D uses the "concluded" note: water moving upward through cracks set off the swarms.

A.why: You picked the method. Placing and monitoring seismometers describes how the study was done, not what the team concluded.

B.why: You picked the aim. This is the question Okafor asked, not the answer the team reached.

C.why: You picked the raw data. A count of recorded earthquakes is an observation. It doesn't say what caused the swarms, and that is what the conclusion explains.

stem: The student wants to present Lindqvist's study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Portolan charts were nautical maps drawn in the Mediterranean region between the 1300s and 1600s.
• Historian Mira Lindqvist wanted to know how accurately the charts depicted coastlines.
• She compared the coastlines on 25 portolan charts with modern satellite maps.
• She found that distances along the charts' coastlines differed from actual distances by an average of only 5 percent.
choices: Lindqvist compared the coastlines drawn on 25 portolan charts with those shown on modern satellite maps.
Comparing 25 portolan charts with satellite maps, Lindqvist found their coastline distances were off by only 5 percent.
Lindqvist wanted to know how accurately portolan charts, drawn between the 1300s and 1600s, depicted coastlines.
Coastline distances on portolan charts differ from actual distances by an average of only about 5 percent.
explanation: "Study and its findings" needs two things: what Lindqvist did and what she found. Choice B names the study (comparing 25 charts with satellite maps) and the result (an average error of only 5 percent).

A.why: You picked a choice that gives only the study's method and never reports what Lindqvist found. The goal asks for both.

C.why: You picked the aim. It states Lindqvist's question but not her study's method or result.

D.why: You picked a choice that gives only the finding. It never mentions Lindqvist or her study, so the reader can't tell where the 5 percent figure came from.

stem: The student wants to present the aim of Kovač's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Brown dwarfs are objects too massive to be planets but too small to sustain hydrogen fusion as stars do.
• In 2023, astronomer Ines Kovač led a team that observed 40 nearby brown dwarfs.
• The team wanted to determine whether brown dwarfs have weather resembling the banded clouds of Jupiter.
• Using infrared telescope data, the team tracked each object's brightness over several hours.
• Of the 40 brown dwarfs, 28 showed brightness changes consistent with rotating cloud bands.
choices: Kovač's team found that 28 of 40 brown dwarfs showed brightness changes consistent with rotating cloud bands.
Kovač's team set out to learn whether brown dwarfs have weather resembling the banded clouds of Jupiter.
Kovač's team used infrared telescope data to track the brightness of 40 brown dwarfs over several hours.
Brown dwarfs are too massive to be planets but too small to sustain hydrogen fusion as stars do.
explanation: The goal asks for the study's aim, meaning what the team wanted to find out. Choice B uses the note about that purpose, and the words 'set out to learn whether' tell the reader it is a question being asked, not an answer being reported.

A.why: You picked the result of the study, not its aim. 'Found that' reports what the team learned, not what it set out to learn.

C.why: You picked the method. This describes how the team gathered data, not the question it was trying to answer.

D.why: You picked the background note. It defines brown dwarfs but says nothing about Kovač's study or its purpose.

stem: The student wants to present Rieder's study and its findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Beavers build dams that slow streams and create ponds.
• Ecologist Tomas Rieder studied 24 streams in Montana: 12 with beaver dams and 12 without.
• Each spring, he counted the amphibian species present at every stream.
• Streams with beaver dams supported an average of six amphibian species.
• Streams without beaver dams supported an average of two amphibian species.
choices: Ecologist Tomas Rieder studied 24 Montana streams, counting the amphibian species at each one every spring.
Streams with beaver dams supported an average of six amphibian species, while others supported only two.
Studying 24 Montana streams, ecologist Tomas Rieder found three times as many amphibian species where beavers had built dams.
Ecologist Tomas Rieder's study showed that amphibians cannot survive in Montana streams without beaver dams.
explanation: The goal asks for two things: the study and what it found. Choice C names the study (Rieder, 24 Montana streams) and its result (three times as many amphibian species at dammed streams, which is six compared with two).

A.why: You picked a choice that describes the study but leaves out its findings. The goal asks for both.

B.why: You picked a choice that gives the findings but never says who did the study or how. The goal asks for the study as well as its results.

D.why: You accepted a claim the notes don't support. Streams without dams still averaged two amphibian species, so the study doesn't show amphibians can't survive there.

stem: The student wants to present the conclusion of Okafor's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some Baroque composers wrote out ornaments such as trills in their scores, while others left them to performers.
• Musicologist Adaeze Okafor examined 60 manuscript copies of keyboard suites by the composer Johann Pflüger.
• She compared ornaments in Pflüger's own hand with those added by later copyists.
• The copyists had added nearly three times as many ornaments as Pflüger wrote.
• Okafor concluded that performances based on the copyists' versions likely sound more ornate than Pflüger intended.
choices: Okafor compared the ornaments in Pflüger's own hand with those that later copyists added to the suites.
Okafor found that later copyists had added nearly three times as many ornaments as Pflüger wrote himself.
Okafor concluded that performances based on copyists' versions likely sound more ornate than Pflüger intended.
Some Baroque composers wrote out trills in their scores, while others left such ornaments to performers.
explanation: The goal asks for the conclusion, meaning what Okafor decided the evidence means. Choice C uses the final note, which goes beyond counting ornaments to say what the count implies for how the music is played today.

A.why: You picked the method. This says what Okafor compared, not what she concluded.

B.why: You picked the finding, not the conclusion. The count of ornaments is the evidence; the conclusion is what Okafor said that evidence means for performers.

D.why: You picked the background. It describes Baroque practice in general and never mentions Okafor's study.

stem: The student wants to present the findings of Varga's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some diet guides advise drinking water with meals to reduce how much people eat.
• Nutrition scientist Lena Varga investigated whether the size of a water cup at lunch affects how much food people eat.
• For four weeks, 80 office workers ate lunch with either a 250-milliliter or a 500-milliliter cup of water.
• Workers given the larger cup ate about 9 percent fewer calories at lunch on average.
choices: Varga investigated whether the size of a lunchtime water cup affects how much food people eat.
Varga gave 80 office workers either a 250-milliliter or a 500-milliliter cup of water at lunch.
Some diet guides advise people to drink water with their meals in order to eat less food.
Varga found that workers given a 500-milliliter cup ate about 9 percent fewer lunch calories.
explanation: The goal asks for the findings, meaning what the study showed. Choice D reports the result: workers with the larger cup ate about 9 percent fewer calories. The word 'found' marks it as a result.

A.why: You picked the aim. 'Investigated whether' states the question Varga asked, not the answer she got.

B.why: You picked the method. It explains how the study was set up but reports no result.

C.why: You picked the background advice. It comes before the study and says nothing about what Varga found.

stem: The student wants to present Ochoa's recommendation to farmers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Cover crops are planted between cash-crop seasons to protect soil.
• Agronomist Rafael Ochoa studied 30 Iowa farms that grew cereal rye as a cover crop.
• He compared farms that ended the rye two weeks before planting soybeans with farms that ended it on planting day.
• Soybean yields were similar in both groups, but farms that waited had less soil erosion.
• Ochoa recommended that farmers keep rye growing until soybean planting day.
choices: Ochoa found that soybean yields were similar whether the rye was ended early or on planting day.
Ochoa advised farmers to keep cereal rye growing until the day they plant their soybean crop.
Ochoa advised farmers to end their cereal rye two weeks before they plant their soybean crop.
Ochoa compared farms that ended rye two weeks early with farms that ended it on planting day.
explanation: The goal asks for a recommendation, which is advice. Choice B uses the last note and states the advice correctly: keep the rye growing until soybean planting day.

A.why: You picked a finding, not the recommendation. Similar yields are part of the evidence behind the advice, not the advice itself.

C.why: You picked a choice that reverses the advice. The farms that ended rye early had more erosion, and Ochoa recommended waiting until planting day.

D.why: You picked the method. It describes the comparison Ochoa made but gives farmers no advice.
